quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 44

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that traffic may enter from a side road ahead.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, what must you show?
questions.explanation: You must have your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in your vehicle at all times. When stopped, you must show all three documents.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists don't have to follow traffic laws.
They will always get a warning.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. If they break traffic laws, they can receive a ticket just like drivers.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
questions.explanation: On a slippery road, first take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with steady, light pressure.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand point upward. What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm points upward, they are signaling that they plan to turn right. Adjust your driving if you see this signal.

questions.question: What does this sign prevent?

options.text: Entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic flows only one way. You cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: Two solid white lines mark a crosswalk. What should you know as a driver?

options.text: Drivers have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
You must give pedestrians the right-of-way in crosswalks.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must give pedestrians the right-of-way in crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to safely cross. You must stop for pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers what they must or must not do. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Construction workers on or near the road.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns that pedestrians may be crossing the road.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver should continue without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.explanation: At four-way stops, all drivers must stop. The driver who reaches the intersection first goes first. If two arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: Your tires work less well as you drive faster.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
The road becomes more slippery when you slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires work less well as you drive faster.
questions.explanation: When you drive faster on wet roads, your tires cannot remove water effectively. If you go too fast, your tires lose grip and you hydroplane—your car slides on a layer of water.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, you should:
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. If you think another driver will hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot enter the road or driveway from your direction. Turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: Drive below the speed limit when:

options.text: You enter a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.explanation: Slow down when the road is wet, you cannot see well, or anything else makes conditions unsafe. You can be ticketed for speeding even if you are at the posted limit when it is unsafe for conditions.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Orange construction signs warn drivers about construction zones. This sign tells you a flagger is ahead and will direct traffic. Follow their directions.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs prepare you for upcoming road hazards. This sign tells you a yield sign is coming. Be ready to stop and let other drivers and pedestrians go first.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus dropping off children:

options.text: Do not go until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking on the roadside. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: The posted speed limit shows:

options.text: The exact speed needed to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed in good road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe speed in all conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed in good road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the highest legal speed for that road. You may need to drive slower than the posted limit. When conditions are poor, slow down.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level above the legal limit can
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving will get worse. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road, you must:

options.text: Flash your lights at oncoming cars.

questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, passing requires good judgment because you must use the oncoming traffic lane to pass safely. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What should you do if your tire blows out?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use your brakes right away.
Slow down gradually and pull to the side of the road.

questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, take your foot off the gas and do not brake immediately. Slow down gradually, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: You are on a freeway and miss your exit. What should you do?

options.text: Make a quick turn from your lane.
Continue driving to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not back up. Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around. It is illegal to back up on a freeway or shoulder.

questions.question: Your accelerator gets stuck while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral and press the brake pedal with steady pressure. When it is safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the accident scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: In an accident, stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: Your right wheels go off the pavement. What should you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the gas, slow down, and gently steer back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas, slow down, and gently steer back onto the road when it is safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, do not panic. Release the gas and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the road by keeping both hands on the wheel and making a small turn. Check for traffic before steering back onto the pavement.

questions.question: When turning left on a multilane, one-way street, which lane should you start from?
questions.explanation: When turning left on a multilane street, start from the left lane.

questions.question: You are driving in an area where children are playing. What should you expect?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful when children are nearby. They may not understand danger and could run in front of you without looking.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with no traffic signals. What should you do?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will never happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At an unmarked railroad crossing, slow down and be ready to stop. Before crossing, make sure no trains are coming from either direction. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance and wait for it to pass.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking your rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Signal three to five seconds before turning left. Check your rearview mirror as you slow down. On a multilane road, move into the left lane before the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then turn when the path is clear.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangular sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign means you must slow down and give the right-of-way to other vehicles and pedestrians. Be ready to stop if necessary.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the road.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show that the road curves sharply in the direction of the arrow. In this case, the road curves to the left. You may see several chevron signs placed along the curve.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of danger ahead. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers they can park for a limited time. When this sign is posted, you may park for a maximum of two hours during the posted times.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can hurt an infant or small child, even in a slow collision.
Always make sure all passengers wear a seat belt or use a child restraint.

questions.explanation: Always wear your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chances of being hurt or killed in a crash. Children age 12 and under must sit properly restrained in the back seat. Never put a rear-facing infant car seat in the front seat of a vehicle with a front passenger airbag.

questions.question: The best way to handle a driver tailgating you is to:

options.text: Speed up to create more space between you.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors every few seconds to watch for tailgaters or fast-approaching vehicles. If a car is following too close, slow down gradually and let it pass. Most rear-end crashes happen when a driver follows too closely.

questions.question: What should concern you most about this sign?

options.text: Your headlights may be misaligned because one side of your car sits higher.
You might damage a tire if you drift onto the shoulder.
Your car might hydroplane if there is water on the shoulder.
You could lose control if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You could lose control if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign means the shoulder is lower than the road. If your wheel drops onto a low shoulder, do not brake hard or turn sharply to get back on the road. This can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and/or flashing lights approaches, you must right away:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights, sirens, or warning devices approaches, drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: What does a green arrow in a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is only used on one-way streets.
It means you can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may only proceed if the green arrow is with a circular green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means you can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow works like a green traffic light. Drivers in that lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers to wait for the left turn signal before turning left. It shows when it is safe to turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead is red.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead is green.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a traffic signal at the next intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns drivers that a playground is near. Watch for children on or near the road.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After the turn, your car should be in:

options.text: The lane with the least traffic.

questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, finish your turn in the lane closest to the lane you just left.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road without bike lanes. A cyclist is ahead of you going the same direction. How should you pass them safely?

options.text: Slow down and wait until no traffic is coming. Then pass the cyclist with plenty of space between you.
Keep driving straight. The cyclist must get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic light or stop sign.
Honk to let the cyclist know you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait until no traffic is coming. Then pass the cyclist with plenty of space between you.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist like you would pass any vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space on regular roads or 5 feet on faster roads. Do not honk unless necessary, as it may startle the cyclist and cause a crash.

questions.question: Orange signs are:
questions.explanation: Orange signs are diamond-shaped with black letters. They warn drivers that construction workers are on or near the highway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Farm machinery may be in the area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farm machinery may be in the area.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns drivers to watch for farm machinery.

questions.question: Signs showing areas for public recreation are what color?
questions.explanation: Brown signs point to places for public recreation and areas with cultural or historical importance. They help when driving in places you do not know.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: It starts to rain while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: When rain reduces visibility, slow down. Turn on your headlights. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see, pull over and stop until it improves.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Be very careful and cross only when you know no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for a train.
Only cross when a flagger signals it is safe.

questions.explanation: Be very careful at all railroad crossings. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their directions.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal traffic laws as if there is no construction.

questions.explanation: Always follow directions from a flagger, sign, or police officer in a construction zone. Ignoring them is illegal and dangerous to workers.
